stages.name: Market Research
stages.objective: Understand market opportunity, competitive landscape, and trends to inform strategy
stages.input: Industry data, competitor information, market reports, customer feedback
stages.output: Market analysis document with opportunity assessment
activities: Competitive research (feature comparison, pricing analysis, messaging study)
TAM/SAM/SOM analysis (total addressable market, serviceable market, obtainable market)
Industry trend identification (emerging technologies, buyer behavior shifts)
Customer research (pain points, buying criteria, success metrics)
Win/loss analysis from sales team
stages.tools: Competitive intelligence platforms, market research databases, industry reports, analyst firms, sales team interviews
stages.successMetric: Comprehensive market understanding documented with data sources cited
decisionPoints: Is the market opportunity large enough to pursue?
What are the top 3-5 competitive threats?
Where are market trends moving?

qualityGate.go: Go if: Market TAM >$1B (or company-specific threshold), competitive landscape clear, trends identified
qualityGate.loopback: Loop back if: Incomplete data, conflicting sources, need primary research

stages.name: Strategic Options Development
stages.objective: Develop 2-3 potential go-to-market approaches with pros/cons
stages.input: Market analysis, company capabilities, product roadmap, financial constraints
stages.output: 2-3 strategic options document with evaluation matrix
activities: Brainstorm go-to-market approaches (inbound-first, outbound-first, land-and-expand, enterprise vs. SMB)
Assess company capabilities (sales team size, marketing budget, product maturity)
Model financial implications (CAC, LTV, payback period for each option)
Scenario planning (best case, base case, worst case for each option)
Risk assessment (competitive response, execution risk, market timing)
stages.tools: Strategy brainstorming tools, financial modeling spreadsheets, scenario planning templates
stages.successMetric: 2-3 options documented with pros/cons analysis and financial modeling
decisionPoints: Which options are realistic given company resources?
Which option has highest ROI potential?
What are the key assumptions underlying each option?

qualityGate.go: Go if: Options are distinct, financial models completed, leadership agreement on viability
qualityGate.loopback: Loop back if: Options are too similar, financial assumptions questioned, need more analysis

stages.name: Strategy Selection
stages.objective: Choose primary GTM strategy and get executive commitment
stages.input: Strategic options, financial modeling, risk assessment, board/leadership input
activities: Executive decision-making session (present options, discuss trade-offs)
Final risk/benefit analysis
Commitment to resource levels and timeline
Documentation of strategy rationale
Communication of decision to extended leadership team
stages.successMetric: Strategy approved by leadership and formally documented
decisionPoints: Which strategy option wins and why?
What resource commitment is required?
When do we reevaluate if conditions change?

qualityGate.go: Go if: Strategy chosen, leadership committed, go/no-go criteria documented
qualityGate.loopback: Loop back if: Leadership unable to decide, need more data, strategic conflict

stages.name: Resource Allocation
stages.objective: Allocate budget, headcount, and tools to execute chosen strategy
stages.input: Approved strategy, financial plan, hiring plan, tool requirements
stages.output: Resource allocation plan with budget locked and hiring initiated
activities: Budget allocation by channel (demand gen, sales, customer success, operations)
Headcount planning (SDRs, AEs, marketers, CSMs, ops roles)
Tool investment planning (CRM, marketing automation, analytics, etc.)
Infrastructure planning (offices, workspace, technology)
Timeline and phasing (Q1-Q4 hiring, budget spend schedule)
stages.tools: Budget tracking spreadsheets, headcount planning tools, HRIS systems
stages.successMetric: Resource plan approved, budget locked, hiring plan initiated
decisionPoints: Are resources sufficient to execute strategy?
What hiring order optimizes ramp?
Which tools are critical vs. nice-to-have?

qualityGate.go: Go if: Budget approved by finance, hiring plan submitted to HR, tools contracted
qualityGate.loopback: Loop back if: Budget constraints, resource unavailable, need to adjust plan

stages.name: Execution Planning
stages.objective: Translate annual strategy into Q1 tactical plan
stages.input: Annual strategy, resources allocated, market priorities
stages.output: Q1 strategic plan with initiatives, OKRs, and team assignments
activities: Quarterly initiative identification (which campaigns, processes, launches in Q1?)
OKR setting (what do we want to achieve in Q1?)
Team assignment (who owns what initiatives?)
Timeline and milestones
Success metrics and tracking setup
stages.tools: OKR frameworks, project management tools, roadmap templates
roles: GTM leadership: initiative and OKR definition
stages.successMetric: Q1 plan documented, OKRs set, team aligned and ready to execute
decisionPoints: Which initiatives should launch in Q1?
What are our stretch vs. committed OKRs?
Do we have dependencies between initiatives?

qualityGate.go: Go if: Plan shared with teams, OKRs approved, kickoff scheduled
qualityGate.loopback: Loop back if: Unclear priorities, resource conflicts, need to adjust plan

stages.name: Quarterly Reviews & Adjustments
stages.objective: Track execution against plan and make strategic adjustments
stages.input: Quarterly results, market changes, competitive updates, learnings
stages.output: Quarterly review with strategy/plan adjustments as needed
activities: Results review (did we hit our OKRs? Why or why not?)
Market monitoring (competitive moves, customer needs shifts)
Learnings extraction (what worked? what didn't? why?)
Resource rebalancing if needed (shift budget/headcount to winning initiatives)
Next quarter planning based on learnings
stages.tools: OKR tracking systems, analytics dashboards, qualitative feedback collection
stages.successMetric: Quarterly review completed, decisions documented, next quarter plan updated
decisionPoints: Should we continue the annual strategy or pivot?
Which initiatives should we double down on?
Where should we shift resources?

qualityGate.go: Go if: Review published to company, learning captured, Q+1 plan started
qualityGate.loopback: Loop back if: Results unclear, need more time for analysis, dependencies unclear

stages.name: Strategy Refinement
stages.objective: Update strategy based on year results and prepare for next year
stages.input: Year results, quarterly reviews, market changes, competitive updates
stages.output: Refined strategy document for next year
activities: Annual strategy review (did our strategy work as planned?)
Market reassessment (market opportunity changed?)
Competitive reassessment (competitive landscape shifted?)
Learning application (what did we learn that changes strategy?)
Next year strategy refinement and documentation
stages.tools: Strategy review frameworks, historical data analysis
roles: Extended team: feedback on what worked/didn't
stages.successMetric: Strategy refined, documented, and approved for next year
decisionPoints: Should we continue the same strategic approach next year?
What did we learn that should change our strategy?
Where should we shift strategic focus?

qualityGate.go: Go if: Next year strategy documented, board approved, budget planning started
qualityGate.loopback: Loop back if: Results need more analysis, strategic consensus unclear

stages.name: Market Scanning
stages.objective: Identify all potential markets and segments company could serve
stages.input: Product capabilities, competitor analysis, market research
activities: Identify potential market segments (by industry, company size, geography, use case)
Research each segment (size, growth, customer profile)
Document current market presence by segment
Identify emerging or underserved segments
stages.tools: Market research platforms, industry databases, analyst reports
stages.successMetric: Comprehensive market/segment list documented
decisionPoints: Which segments are we not currently serving?
Are there emerging segments with growth potential?

qualityGate.go: Go if: 10+ segments identified and researched
qualityGate.loopback: Loop back if: Incomplete research, missing key segments

stages.name: Opportunity Identification
stages.objective: Assess opportunity level for each potential market
stages.input: Segment list, market sizing data, competitive data
stages.output: Scored opportunity list with high/medium/low potential
activities: Score each segment on: size, growth, customer fit, competitive intensity
Identify adjacent segments (different customer profile, same use case)
Assess customer pain points in each segment
Identify customer buying journey for each segment
stages.successMetric: Opportunity scored for each segment, ranked by potential
decisionPoints: Which segments have the best fit with our product?
Which segments are growing fastest?
Which segments have least competition?

qualityGate.go: Go if: All segments scored consistently, ranking agreed upon
qualityGate.loopback: Loop back if: Scoring criteria unclear, need more data

stages.name: Market Sizing
stages.objective: Calculate market size and addressable market for prioritized segments
stages.input: Opportunity-ranked segments, market research data
stages.output: Market sizing for top segments (TAM, SAM, SOM)
activities: Calculate TAM (Total Addressable Market) - all customers who could buy
Calculate SAM (Serviceable Available Market) - customers we can realistically reach
Calculate SOM (Serviceable Obtainable Market) - what we can capture in year 1-3
Identify market growth rate and trends
Assess market maturity (emerging, growth, mature, decline)
stages.tools: Market research databases, analyst reports, spreadsheet modeling
stages.successMetric: Market sizes calculated for top 3-5 segments with growth rates
decisionPoints: Which segments have large enough markets?
Is the market growing or contracting?
Can we realistically capture meaningful market share?

qualityGate.go: Go if: TAM/SAM/SOM calculated, growth rates verified, methodology documented
qualityGate.loopback: Loop back if: Data insufficient, methodology questioned

stages.name: Competitive Assessment
stages.objective: Assess competitive landscape within each target segment
stages.input: Top-ranked segments, competitor data
stages.output: Competitive analysis by segment with positioning recommendations
activities: Identify competitors in each segment
Assess competitor strength, positioning, and market share
Identify competitive gaps and weaknesses
Assess barriers to entry and how defensible competitive position is
stages.tools: Competitive intelligence tools, sales win/loss data
stages.successMetric: Competitive analysis completed for each target segment
decisionPoints: Which segments have less competitive intensity?
Where can we build defensible competitive advantage?
Which competitors are strongest in each segment?

qualityGate.go: Go if: Competitors identified, positioning clear, gaps documented
qualityGate.loopback: Loop back if: Incomplete competitor research, need more depth

stages.name: Prioritization
stages.objective: Rank segments by overall attractiveness and fit
stages.input: Opportunity scores, market sizes, competitive analysis
activities: Score segments on: TAM size, growth rate, competitive intensity, product fit, customer fit
Weight scoring factors based on company strategy
Rank segments overall
Define Tier 1 (focus), Tier 2 (build), Tier 3 (monitor)
Get leadership alignment on prioritization
stages.successMetric: Prioritized segment list with clear Tier 1/2/3 definition
decisionPoints: What's our top segment to focus on?
What's our secondary/tertiary focus?
Should we specialize in 1-2 segments or go broad?

qualityGate.go: Go if: Prioritization agreed by leadership, rationale documented
qualityGate.loopback: Loop back if: Conflict on prioritization, need more consensus

stages.name: Segment Definition
stages.objective: Deeply define target customer profile for each prioritized segment
stages.input: Prioritized segments, customer research data
stages.output: Detailed segment/ICP definition with customer profile, pain points, buying criteria
activities: Define ideal customer profile (company size, industry, use cases, geography)
Document customer pain points and success metrics
Map customer buying journey (who are decision-makers, what's their process?)
Identify customer motivations and objections
Create segment-specific messaging and positioning
stages.tools: Customer research tools, persona development frameworks
roles: Customer success: customer pain points and success metrics
stages.successMetric: Detailed ICP documented for each Tier 1 segment
decisionPoints: Who is our ideal customer in each segment?
What's their buying process?
What are their key decision criteria?

qualityGate.go: Go if: ICP definition complete, buying journey mapped, messaging started
qualityGate.loopback: Loop back if: Customer understanding insufficient, need more research

stages.name: Go-to-Market Planning
stages.objective: Develop segment-specific GTM strategy and tactics
stages.input: Segment definition, competitive positioning, resource availability
stages.output: Segment-specific GTM plan with channel strategy, messaging, and tactics
activities: Define channel strategy (inbound, outbound, partnerships, events for each segment)
Develop segment-specific messaging and positioning
Plan customer acquisition approach (how do we reach this segment?)
Identify customer advocates or reference customers
Set segment-specific targets and forecasts
stages.tools: GTM planning templates, channel strategy frameworks
stages.successMetric: Segment-specific GTM plan documented with targets
decisionPoints: Which channels are most effective for this segment?
What's our customer acquisition strategy?
What do we need to succeed in this segment?

qualityGate.go: Go if: GTM plan complete, channels selected, targets set, execution plan ready
qualityGate.loopback: Loop back if: Unclear strategy, resource gaps, need clarification

stages.name: Competitive Research
stages.objective: Understand competitive landscape, product features, and positioning
stages.input: Competitor list, industry data, customer feedback
stages.output: Competitive analysis document with feature/pricing/messaging comparison
activities: Research competitor products (features, capabilities, limitations)
Research competitor pricing (tiers, pricing strategy, value positioning)
Research competitor messaging (value prop, positioning, target market)
Research competitor go-to-market (channels, customer acquisition, sales process)
Analyze win/loss data to understand why customers choose competitors
stages.tools: Competitive intelligence platforms, competitor websites, sales win/loss database
stages.successMetric: Competitive analysis documented with detailed comparison
decisionPoints: Who are our top 3-5 competitors?
What features do they have that we don't?
How do they position differently than us?

qualityGate.go: Go if: Top competitors analyzed, features compared, messaging documented
qualityGate.loopback: Loop back if: Incomplete research, missing key competitors

stages.name: Positioning Analysis
stages.objective: Analyze where competitors position and identify gaps
stages.input: Competitive analysis, market research, customer research
stages.output: Positioning gap analysis with opportunity identification
activities: Map competitor positioning on a 2D matrix (e.g., enterprise vs. SMB, price vs. features)
Identify positioning gaps (where no competitor is strong)
Assess defensibility of gaps (can we own this space?)
Identify adjacent positioning moves (if we move here, can we win?)
Assess customer perception of our current positioning vs. competitors
stages.successMetric: Positioning gaps identified with feasibility analysis
decisionPoints: Where can we own a unique position?
What position is defensible and valuable?
Should we move our positioning or stay put?

qualityGate.go: Go if: Gaps mapped, opportunities identified, customer validation started
qualityGate.loopback: Loop back if: Gaps unclear, feasibility questioned

stages.name: Message Development
stages.objective: Develop core differentiating messages
stages.input: Positioning analysis, company capabilities, market research
stages.output: Key messages and value propositions validated by customers
activities: Develop core value proposition (what we do differently and better)
Develop supporting messages (specific benefits, use cases)
Develop anti-messages (what we're NOT)
Test messages with target customers
Refine based on feedback
Develop messaging variants for different personas/segments
stages.tools: Messaging frameworks, customer research, A/B testing
stages.successMetric: Core messages developed and tested with customers
decisionPoints: What message resonates most with customers?
Is our differentiation compelling and believable?
Do we need different messages for different segments?

qualityGate.go: Go if: Messages tested and validated, customer feedback positive, ready for sales training
qualityGate.loopback: Loop back if: Messages not resonating, need to adjust

stages.name: Differentiation Strategy
stages.objective: Define how we're different and better than competitors
stages.input: Messages, positioning, competitive positioning, product capabilities
stages.output: Differentiation strategy document linking features to benefits to value
activities: Map company features to customer benefits
Map benefits to customer value/ROI
Compare differentiation vs. competitors
Develop ROI arguments for differentiation
Identify which differentiators matter most to customers
stages.successMetric: Differentiation strategy documented with feature/benefit/value linkage
decisionPoints: What are our top 3-5 differentiators?
Which differentiators drive customer buying decisions?
Can we prove our differentiation claims?

qualityGate.go: Go if: Differentiation clear and defensible, ROI quantified, customer validated
qualityGate.loopback: Loop back if: Differentiation questionable, can't prove claims

stages.name: Messaging Hierarchy
stages.objective: Organize messages from primary to tertiary by priority
stages.input: Differentiation strategy, customer research, persona segmentation
stages.output: Messaging hierarchy by persona and customer journey stage
activities: Rank messages by importance (primary, secondary, tertiary)
Develop persona-specific messaging (what messages matter to each buyer persona?)
Develop journey-specific messaging (what messages matter at awareness vs. consideration vs. decision?)
Create messaging frameworks for different scenarios (objection handling, comparison, value prop)
Document messaging guidelines for sales and marketing
stages.successMetric: Messaging hierarchy documented by persona/journey with clear priority
decisionPoints: Which message should we lead with?
Do we need different messages for different personas?
How do we simplify without losing important nuance?

qualityGate.go: Go if: Hierarchy documented, sales/marketing aligned, training materials ready
qualityGate.loopback: Loop back if: Hierarchy unclear, personas need refinement

stages.name: Sales/Marketing Alignment
stages.objective: Ensure sales and marketing use consistent messaging
stages.input: Messaging hierarchy, sales playbooks, marketing materials
stages.output: Aligned sales and marketing materials with consistent messaging
activities: Audit current sales materials (presentations, battle cards, emails)
Audit current marketing materials (website, ads, content, emails)
Update materials to align with new messaging hierarchy
Train sales team on new messaging
Train marketing team on messaging guidelines
Create collateral (one-pagers, pitch decks, battle cards) with aligned messaging
Establish feedback loop for messaging updates
stages.tools: Sales training platforms, marketing asset management
stages.successMetric: All sales and marketing materials updated and aligned, sales trained
decisionPoints: Are sales and marketing using the same messages?
Do materials reflect the messaging hierarchy?
Is the sales team adopting the new messaging?

qualityGate.go: Go if: Materials audited and updated, sales trained and adopting, customer feedback positive
qualityGate.loopback: Loop back if: Adoption low, materials need more updates

stages.name: Continuous Monitoring
stages.objective: Track competitive changes and messaging effectiveness
stages.input: Win/loss data, customer feedback, competitive updates, marketing metrics
activities: Track win/loss data (are we winning or losing to competitors? Why?)
Monitor customer feedback (is our messaging resonating?)
Monitor competitor moves (are they changing their positioning?)
Monitor marketing metrics (are messages driving engagement and conversions?)
Quarterly positioning review (should we adjust?)
stages.tools: Win/loss database, customer feedback tools, competitive intelligence, analytics
stages.successMetric: Positioning reviewed quarterly, updates made as needed, stays competitive
decisionPoints: Should we adjust our positioning?
Are competitors gaining ground in any area?
Is our messaging still relevant and resonating?

qualityGate.go: Go if: Monitoring system in place, quarterly reviews happening, responsive to changes
qualityGate.loopback: Loop back if: Not monitoring effectively, missed competitive moves

stages.name: GTM Needs Assessment
stages.objective: Identify what GTM needs from product roadmap
stages.input: Market priorities, customer feedback, competitive gaps, sales feedback
stages.output: GTM feature priorities and timing requirements
stages.activities: Gather GTM feedback on customer needs, competitive gaps, sales wins/losses, market requirements
stages.successMetric: Clear GTM feature priorities documented with timing
stages.decisionPoints: What features most impact GTM success? Timeline critical?

stages.name: Product Requirements
stages.objective: Translate GTM needs into product requirements
stages.input: GTM priorities, product capabilities, technical constraints
stages.output: Product requirements document for roadmap features
stages.activities: Define requirements detail, assess technical feasibility, identify dependencies, estimate effort
stages.successMetric: Product requirements clear and feasible
stages.decisionPoints: Requirements address GTM needs? Technical feasible? Timeline realistic?
stages.qualityGate: Requirements documented, engineering feasibility confirmed, timeline agreed

stages.name: Release Planning
stages.objective: Plan release cadence and feature sequencing
stages.input: Product requirements, engineering capacity, market timing
stages.activities: Sequence features by priority/timing, plan releases (quarterly, monthly, etc.), identify dependencies, confirm capacity
stages.successMetric: Release roadmap documented with feature timing
stages.decisionPoints: Release cadence? Feature sequencing? Market timing critical?
stages.qualityGate: Roadmap approved, GTM and engineering aligned, timeline confirmed

stages.name: Launch Strategy
stages.objective: Develop go-to-market strategy for new features/releases
stages.input: Release roadmap, market priorities, competitive positioning
stages.output: Launch plan with messaging, targeting, channels
stages.activities: Define launch timing, develop launch messaging, plan target audience, identify launch channels, plan customer communication
stages.successMetric: Launch plan documented with messaging and channels
stages.decisionPoints: Launch timing optimal? Messaging compelling? Channels selected?
stages.qualityGate: Launch plan complete, messaging approved, channels aligned

stages.name: Go-to-Market Execution
stages.objective: Execute launch and drive feature adoption
stages.input: Launch plan approved, launch messaging ready
stages.output: Live launch with adoption metrics tracked
stages.activities: Execute launch campaigns, drive awareness, support sales, track adoption, monitor customer feedback
stages.successMetric: Launch executed, adoption metrics tracked, customer feedback positive
stages.decisionPoints: Launch timing optimal? Adoption tracking? Customer response?
stages.qualityGate: Launch complete, adoption metrics tracked, feedback collected

stages.name: Customer Feedback
stages.objective: Gather customer feedback on new features
stages.input: Feature live, customer usage data
stages.activities: Collect customer feedback, analyze usage data, identify feature issues, identify adoption barriers
stages.successMetric: Customer feedback documented, adoption patterns clear
stages.decisionPoints: Feature resonating? Adoption as expected? Issues identified?
stages.qualityGate: Feedback collected, usage analyzed, learning documented

stages.name: Roadmap Refinement
stages.objective: Update roadmap based on feature performance and feedback
stages.input: Customer feedback, adoption data, market response
stages.activities: Assess feature performance, update priorities based on impact, identify next features, adjust roadmap
stages.successMetric: Roadmap refined based on learning, priorities updated
stages.decisionPoints: Features underperforming? Should we adjust priorities? Next focus?
stages.qualityGate: Roadmap updated, GTM aligned on next priorities

stages.name: Customer Research
stages.objective: Understand customer willingness to pay and value perception
stages.input: Customer data, market research, sales feedback
stages.activities: Interview customers on pricing, survey willingness to pay, analyze customer value perception, research customer buying criteria
stages.tools: Customer research, survey tools, pricing research
stages.roles: Pricing strategy lead, Customer success (feedback), Sales (data)
stages.successMetric: Willingness to pay understood for each segment
stages.decisionPoints: How much would customers pay? Value drivers? Segment variations?
stages.qualityGate: Customer research complete, willingness to pay clear

stages.name: Value Analysis
stages.objective: Quantify value delivered by product to customers
stages.input: Customer success data, ROI calculations, competitive benchmarking
stages.activities: Calculate customer ROI, identify value drivers, estimate time to value, assess value by segment
stages.roles: Pricing strategy lead, Finance, Customer success
stages.successMetric: Value quantified for each segment/customer type
stages.decisionPoints: How to measure value? ROI by customer? Value drivers?
stages.qualityGate: Value quantified and validated with customers

stages.name: Competitive Benchmarking
stages.objective: Understand competitive pricing and positioning
stages.input: Competitor pricing data, market research, sales competitive feedback
stages.activities: Research competitor pricing, assess competitive positioning, identify pricing gaps, understand pricing strategies
stages.tools: Competitive intelligence, pricing databases, sales win/loss
stages.successMetric: Competitive pricing landscape understood
stages.decisionPoints: How do we position vs. competitors? Pricing gap opportunities? Premium or value?

stages.name: Pricing Model Design
stages.objective: Design optimal pricing model for business
stages.input: Value analysis, willingness to pay, competitive benchmarking
stages.activities: Model different pricing approaches (value-based, cost-plus, competitive, freemium, usage-based), compare financial impact, select optimal model
stages.roles: Pricing strategy lead, Finance, Executive team
stages.successMetric: Pricing model designed with financial modeling
stages.decisionPoints: Value-based or cost-based? Per-seat or usage? Premium or discount vs. competitors?
stages.qualityGate: Pricing model selected, financial modeling complete, leadership agreement

stages.name: Packaging Architecture
stages.objective: Design pricing tiers and feature bundling
stages.input: Pricing model, feature set, customer segmentation
stages.output: Packaging architecture with tiers and features
stages.activities: Define tiers (starter/professional/enterprise), allocate features by tier, set price points, plan add-ons
stages.successMetric: Packaging architecture defined with price points
stages.decisionPoints: How many tiers? Which features per tier? Add-ons for revenue?
stages.qualityGate: Packaging approved, price points set, feature allocation clear

stages.name: Testing
stages.objective: Test pricing approach with customers and market
stages.input: Packaging architecture, customer sample
stages.activities: Test pricing with customer sample, gather feedback on perceived value, refine based on feedback, test pricing page conversions
stages.roles: Pricing strategy lead, Sales (feedback), Marketing (landing pages)
stages.successMetric: Pricing tested and validated with customers
stages.decisionPoints: Price points resonating? Feature allocation make sense? Add-ons valuable?
stages.qualityGate: Pricing tested, customer feedback positive, ready to implement

stages.name: Optimization
stages.objective: Continuously optimize pricing strategy
stages.input: Pricing live, customer data, competitive updates
stages.activities: Monitor pricing conversion, analyze customer value realization, track competitive pricing, gather customer feedback, recommend optimizations
stages.successMetric: Pricing monitored and optimized regularly
stages.decisionPoints: Are price points optimal? Should we adjust? Competitive moves to counter?
stages.qualityGate: Pricing optimization cadence established, improvements made based on data

stages.name: Account Universe Definition
stages.objective: Identify all accounts that could be assigned to territories
stages.input: ICP definition, market data, current customer list
stages.output: Comprehensive account universe with fit scoring
stages.activities: Identify potential accounts, score fit to ICP, estimate account value, segment by size/type
stages.tools: Account databases, CRM, fit scoring tools
stages.successMetric: Complete account universe with fit scoring
stages.decisionPoints: How many accounts total? What's our total addressable?

stages.name: Account Segmentation
stages.objective: Segment accounts by opportunity and coverage strategy
stages.input: Account universe, fit scoring, revenue potential
stages.activities: Segment by size/opportunity, identify tier 1/2/3 accounts, plan coverage model (1:1, 1:many, digital), identify expansion opportunities
stages.successMetric: Accounts segmented with coverage strategy
stages.decisionPoints: How many tiers? Coverage approach? Expansion strategy?

stages.name: Capacity Planning
stages.objective: Assess sales team capacity and plan hiring
stages.input: Account universe, target revenue, current headcount
stages.activities: Calculate accounts per rep, assess current capacity, model hiring needed, plan onboarding timeline
stages.successMetric: Capacity model complete with hiring plan
stages.decisionPoints: Accounts per rep sustainable? Hiring needed? Timeline?
stages.qualityGate: Capacity assessment complete, hiring plan aligned

stages.name: Territory Design
stages.objective: Design territories that are balanced and achievable
stages.input: Segmentation, capacity plan, account locations
stages.activities: Create territories (geographic, account-based, vertical-based), balance across reps, account assignment, document territory rules
stages.successMetric: Territories designed and balanced
stages.decisionPoints: Geographic or account-based territories? How balanced? Clear rules?
stages.qualityGate: Territory design approved, account assignments clear

stages.name: Rep Assignment
stages.objective: Assign reps to territories matching capability
stages.input: Territory design, rep profiles, capabilities
stages.activities: Assess rep capabilities, match to territories, plan onboarding, document assignments
stages.successMetric: All territories assigned with aligned reps
stages.decisionPoints: Right rep for right territory? Capability gaps? Onboarding plan?
stages.qualityGate: Assignments complete, reps notified, onboarding planned

stages.name: Quota Setting
stages.objective: Set revenue quotas for each rep and territory
stages.input: Territory accounts, historical data, revenue targets
stages.activities: Analyze historical performance by territory, estimate revenue potential per territory, set quotas, plan for new reps/territories
stages.successMetric: Quotas set for all reps, aligned to company revenue goals
stages.decisionPoints: Quotas realistic? Aligned to historical performance? Fair distribution?
stages.qualityGate: Quotas approved by leadership, communicated to reps

stages.name: Performance Tracking
stages.objective: Track territory and rep performance throughout year
stages.input: Quotas, performance data, account data
stages.activities: Track quota attainment, identify high/low performers, provide coaching, adjust resources as needed
stages.tools: CRM dashboards, pipeline analytics, coaching tools
stages.successMetric: Performance tracked monthly, coaching provided
stages.decisionPoints: Who's on track? Who needs support? Resource shifts needed?

stages.name: Rebalancing
stages.objective: Rebalance territories if needed based on performance/changes
stages.input: Performance data, headcount changes, market changes
stages.output: Territory adjustments or new territory design
stages.activities: Assess territory balance, identify underperforming territories, make adjustments, communicate changes
stages.successMetric: Territories rebalanced when needed, adjustments communicated
stages.decisionPoints: Rebalance needed? Account shifts? New assignments?
stages.qualityGate: Rebalancing done annually or when major changes occur

stages.name: Demand Forecasting
stages.objective: Forecast GTM resource needs for year
stages.input: Annual strategy, growth targets, initiatives planned
stages.activities: Forecast leads needed by channel, forecast sales capacity needed, forecast marketing capacity, forecast customer success capacity
stages.successMetric: Resource demand forecast completed
stages.decisionPoints: How many leads do we need? Sales capacity? Support capacity?

stages.name: Capability Gap Analysis
stages.objective: Identify gaps between current capabilities and forecasted demand
stages.input: Current headcount, demand forecast, capability requirements
stages.activities: Compare current vs. needed capabilities, identify skill gaps, identify headcount gaps, assess team strengths/weaknesses
stages.successMetric: Capability gaps identified and quantified
stages.decisionPoints: Headcount gaps? Skill gaps? Build vs. buy?

stages.name: Hiring Plan
stages.objective: Plan hiring to close capability gaps
stages.input: Capability gaps, budget available, hiring timeline
stages.output: Annual hiring plan with roles, timing, budget
stages.activities: Define roles needed, plan hiring sequence, estimate hiring costs, plan onboarding, communicate hiring plan
stages.successMetric: Hiring plan documented with roles and timeline
stages.decisionPoints: Roles to hire? Hiring order? Budget sufficient?
stages.qualityGate: Hiring plan approved by leadership and finance, HR alignment

stages.name: Budget Allocation
stages.objective: Allocate budget to GTM functions and initiatives
stages.input: Demand forecast, hiring plan, tool requirements, initiative budgets
stages.output: GTM budget allocation by function and initiative
stages.activities: Allocate budget by function (demand gen, sales, success, ops), allocate contingency, plan spend timeline
stages.successMetric: Budget allocated and approved
stages.decisionPoints: Budget distribution? Contingency allocation? Flexibility?
stages.qualityGate: Budget approved by finance, spend plan documented

stages.name: Tool Investment
stages.objective: Plan tool/technology investments needed
stages.input: Initiative requirements, current tool stack, budget available
stages.output: Tool investment plan with priorities and budget
stages.activities: Assess current tools, identify gaps, evaluate new tools, plan implementation, allocate budget
stages.successMetric: Tool investment plan documented with budget
stages.decisionPoints: Which tools critical? Implementation timeline? Vendor selection?
stages.qualityGate: Tool investment approved, vendors identified, implementation planned

stages.name: Execution
stages.objective: Execute hiring and resource allocation throughout year
stages.input: Hiring plan, budget allocation, resource plan
stages.activities: Recruit and hire, onboard new employees, allocate to projects, deploy resources
stages.successMetric: Hiring on track, resources deployed, onboarding complete
stages.decisionPoints: Hiring pace on track? Resources deployed effectively? Ramp curves expected?
stages.qualityGate: Hiring and deployment on track, no critical staffing gaps

stages.name: Utilization Tracking
stages.objective: Track resource utilization and efficiency
stages.input: Resource deployed, project hours tracked, productivity data
stages.activities: Track time allocation, measure productivity, identify over/under-utilization, gather feedback
stages.successMetric: Utilization tracked monthly, trends visible
stages.decisionPoints: Utilization optimal? Productivity up to expectation? Rebalancing needed?
stages.qualityGate: Utilization tracking in place, regular reviews happening

stages.name: Optimization
stages.objective: Optimize resource allocation based on performance
stages.input: Utilization data, performance metrics, team feedback
stages.activities: Analyze utilization vs. results, identify inefficiencies, recommend optimizations, adjust allocation
stages.successMetric: Resource optimization recommendations documented
stages.decisionPoints: Resource allocation optimal? Capability gaps closed? Team effective?
stages.qualityGate: Quarterly optimization review, adjustments made as needed

stages.name: Revenue Target Definition
stages.objective: Define revenue targets for year
stages.input: Company growth goals, market opportunity, historical performance
stages.activities: Set annual revenue target, break into quarterly targets, set targets by segment/product, document rationale
stages.roles: Executive leadership (targets), Finance (validation), GTM leadership (feasibility assessment)
stages.successMetric: Revenue targets set for year and quarters
stages.decisionPoints: Revenue target achievable? Aligned to market opportunity? By segment breakdown?
stages.qualityGate: Revenue targets approved by leadership and board

stages.name: Conversion Rate Modeling
stages.objective: Model conversion rates by sales stage
stages.input: Historical conversion data, sales process, pipeline behavior
stages.activities: Analyze historical conversion rates by stage, identify benchmarks, model forward, assess assumptions
stages.tools: Analytics tools, historical data, pipeline tools
stages.successMetric: Conversion rates modeled for each stage
stages.decisionPoints: Conversion rates realistic? Any improvements expected?

stages.name: Pipeline Requirements
stages.objective: Calculate pipeline needed to hit revenue targets
stages.input: Revenue targets, conversion rates
stages.activities: Calculate pipeline needed at each stage, work backwards from revenue target, assess current vs. needed
stages.successMetric: Pipeline requirements calculated
stages.decisionPoints: Current pipeline sufficient? New pipeline needed? By how much?

stages.name: Forecast Build
stages.objective: Build revenue forecast based on current pipeline
stages.input: Current pipeline, pipeline requirements, conversion rates
stages.activities: Model current pipeline through conversion rates, identify forecast gap, build pipeline addition needed
stages.successMetric: Revenue forecast documented
stages.decisionPoints: Forecast to hit targets? Gap identified? Risks?

stages.name: Risk Assessment
stages.objective: Identify risks to revenue forecast
stages.input: Revenue forecast, pipeline data, market factors
stages.activities: Identify pipeline risks (loss rates, stage time), identify competitive risks, identify market risks, quantify impact
stages.roles: Sales leadership (pipeline risk), GTM (market risk), Finance (impact)
stages.successMetric: Risks identified and quantified
stages.decisionPoints: What's our biggest forecast risk? Impact if realized? Mitigation possible?

stages.name: Mitigation Planning
stages.objective: Plan mitigation for identified risks
stages.input: Risk assessment, pipeline, resources available
stages.activities: Plan mitigations for top risks, plan contingencies, ensure resource availability
stages.successMetric: Mitigation plan for top risks documented
stages.decisionPoints: Mitigations sufficient? Additional resources needed?

stages.name: Tracking
stages.objective: Track pipeline and forecast performance throughout year
stages.input: Revenue forecast, current pipeline, monthly results
stages.activities: Monitor pipeline health, compare actual to forecast, update forecast monthly, assess forecast accuracy
stages.tools: CRM dashboards, forecasting tools, pipeline analytics
stages.successMetric: Pipeline and forecast tracked monthly with visibility
stages.decisionPoints: On track to forecast? Variance from plan? Forecast adjusted?
stages.qualityGate: Monthly tracking happening, forecast updates communicated

stages.name: Adjustment
stages.objective: Adjust pipeline and forecast based on performance
stages.input: Tracking data, market changes, pipeline changes
stages.activities: Analyze variances, adjust forecast as needed, adjust pipeline strategy, rebalance resources
stages.successMetric: Forecast adjusted, strategy updated
stages.decisionPoints: Major adjustments needed? Strategy shift? Resource rebalancing?

stages.name: Segment Definition
stages.objective: Define which segment/persona the playbook targets
stages.input: ICP definition, segment analysis, customer data
stages.activities: Define target segment, customer profile, pain points, success criteria, buying journey
stages.successMetric: Clear segment/persona defined
stages.decisionPoints: One playbook or multiple by segment? Level of detail?

stages.name: Use Case Mapping
stages.objective: Identify how our product solves customer problems in this segment
stages.input: Segment definition, product capabilities, customer pain points
stages.activities: Map customer pain points to our solutions, identify key use cases, quantify value/ROI, identify competitive alternatives
stages.successMetric: Use cases mapped with value quantified
stages.decisionPoints: What are top 3 use cases? ROI clear? Differentiated?

stages.name: Messaging Development
stages.objective: Develop segment-specific messaging and positioning
stages.input: Use cases, competitive positioning, segment needs
stages.output: Segment messaging with primary, secondary, supporting messages
stages.activities: Develop value propositions, develop supporting messages, develop objection handling messages
stages.successMetric: Segment messaging developed and validated
stages.decisionPoints: Messaging resonates? Differentiated from competitors?
stages.qualityGate: Messaging approved by sales and marketing leadership

stages.name: Objection Identification
stages.objective: Identify and plan for common objections in this segment
stages.input: Win/loss analysis, sales feedback, competitive data
stages.activities: Identify top objections, develop handling responses, plan for competitive objections, develop proof points
stages.successMetric: Top objections identified with responses documented
stages.decisionPoints: Most common objections? Best responses? Case studies to support?

stages.name: Solution Architecture
stages.objective: Map product to customer solution architecture
stages.input: Use cases, customer technical context, product capabilities
stages.activities: Define typical customer architecture, map product into it, identify integrations, plan technical positioning
stages.successMetric: Solution architecture clear for segment
stages.decisionPoints: How does product fit customer tech stack? Key integrations?

stages.name: Playbook Creation
stages.objective: Create comprehensive playbook for sales to follow
stages.input: Messaging, use cases, objections, solution architecture, sales process
stages.activities: Document segment strategy, document sales process by stage, document key messages/talking points, document case studies/proof points, document tools/resources
stages.successMetric: Comprehensive playbook documented
stages.decisionPoints: Enough detail without being overwhelming? Organized clearly?
stages.qualityGate: Playbook complete, reviewed by sales leadership

stages.name: Sales Enablement
stages.objective: Train sales team on playbook and get adoption
stages.input: Completed playbook
stages.output: Trained sales team with playbook adoption
stages.activities: Conduct training session, role-play scenarios, provide feedback, establish usage expectations, create accountability
stages.successMetric: Sales team trained, adoption beginning
stages.decisionPoints: Adoption level? Gaps in understanding? Additional support needed?

stages.name: Iteration
stages.objective: Update playbook based on sales feedback and results
stages.input: Sales feedback, win/loss data, usage data
stages.activities: Gather sales feedback on playbook, analyze results, identify gaps/improvements, update playbook, retrain
stages.successMetric: Playbook updated quarterly based on learning
stages.decisionPoints: What's working? What needs improvement? Major changes or tweaks?
stages.qualityGate: Regular playbook reviews happening, improvements implemented

stages.name: Annual Theme Definition
stages.objective: Define overarching marketing theme/strategy for year
stages.input: Annual GTM strategy, market positioning, customer needs
stages.activities: Define annual theme, define 3-5 marketing pillars/topics, identify key moments/events, plan messaging flow
stages.successMetric: Clear annual theme with 3-5 pillars
stages.decisionPoints: Compelling theme? Aligned to strategy? Flexible enough for changes?

stages.name: Campaign Identification
stages.objective: Identify specific campaigns for the year
stages.input: Annual theme, quarterly OKRs, customer calendar, industry calendar
stages.activities: Identify demand gen campaigns, identify engagement campaigns, identify thought leadership campaigns, identify event tie-ins
stages.successMetric: Campaign calendar with campaigns identified
stages.decisionPoints: Right number of campaigns? Good distribution throughout year? Aligned to OKRs?

stages.name: Content Planning
stages.objective: Plan content needed to support campaigns and pillars
stages.input: Campaign calendar, marketing pillars, content inventory
stages.output: Content calendar with content pieces identified
stages.activities: Identify content pieces by type (blog, whitepaper, case study, video, etc.), plan content creation, identify repurposing opportunities
stages.successMetric: Content calendar with all campaigns and content mapped
stages.decisionPoints: Right content mix? Creation vs. repurposing? Enough resources?

stages.name: Channel Allocation
stages.objective: Allocate campaigns and content to channels
stages.input: Campaign calendar, content calendar, channel capabilities
stages.activities: Map campaigns to channels, identify channel owners, plan channel strategy for each campaign
stages.successMetric: Campaigns and content allocated to channels
stages.decisionPoints: Right channels for each campaign? Resource available? Conflicts?
stages.qualityGate: Channel allocation complete, channel leads aligned

stages.name: Timeline Creation
stages.objective: Create detailed timeline for campaign execution
stages.input: Campaign calendar, content calendar, channel allocation
stages.output: Detailed timeline with milestones and deadlines
stages.activities: Define campaign start/end dates, identify key milestones, identify content creation deadlines, identify publishing dates
stages.successMetric: Detailed timeline with all milestones
stages.decisionPoints: Timeline realistic? Enough lead time? Dependencies clear?

stages.name: Resource Assignment
stages.objective: Assign resources to each campaign and content piece
stages.input: Timeline, campaigns, content, available resources
stages.output: Resource allocation with owners and team assignments
stages.activities: Assign campaign owners, assign content creators, assign budget, plan resource timeline
stages.successMetric: All campaigns and content assigned owners with resources confirmed
stages.decisionPoints: Resources sufficient? Right skills assigned? Capacity conflicts?

stages.name: Publishing Schedule
stages.objective: Create detailed publishing schedule for content
stages.input: Content calendar, channel allocation, timeline
stages.activities: Define publishing dates and frequency, identify publishing channel per content, set up automation where possible
stages.successMetric: Publishing schedule defined for all content
stages.decisionPoints: Publishing frequency optimal? Timezone considerations? Promotion timing?
stages.qualityGate: Publishing schedule confirmed, automation set up

stages.name: Performance Tracking
stages.objective: Track marketing calendar execution and performance
stages.input: Publishing schedule, campaigns active
stages.activities: Monitor campaign performance, track content engagement, track channel performance, identify optimizations needed
stages.successMetric: Performance tracked monthly, reporting consistent
stages.decisionPoints: Campaigns on track? Content performing? Optimizations needed?
stages.qualityGate: Performance tracking in place, regular reviews happening

stages.name: Priority Setting
stages.objective: Identify top priorities for week/month
stages.input: OKRs, initiatives, customer needs, blockers
stages.activities: Review OKRs and initiatives, identify top 3-5 priorities for week, identify urgent issues, plan priority order
stages.successMetric: Clear top priorities identified
stages.decisionPoints: What's most important this week? Any urgent items? Dependencies?

stages.name: Task Definition
stages.objective: Break priorities into specific tasks
stages.input: Priorities identified
stages.activities: Define specific tasks for each priority, break into subtasks, define success criteria
stages.successMetric: All priorities broken into specific tasks
stages.decisionPoints: Tasks clear and actionable? Right level of detail?

stages.name: Owner Assignment
stages.objective: Assign owners to each task
stages.input: Task list, team capabilities
stages.activities: Identify task owners, confirm capacity, establish accountability
stages.successMetric: All tasks assigned with confirmed owners
stages.decisionPoints: Right person for each task? Capacity okay? Too many on one person?

stages.name: Deadline Setting
stages.objective: Set realistic deadlines for each task
stages.input: Task list, owner assignments
stages.activities: Set deadlines, sequence tasks, identify dependencies, plan buffer time
stages.successMetric: All tasks have deadlines
stages.decisionPoints: Deadlines realistic? Dependencies sequenced? Buffers adequate?

stages.name: Resource Allocation
stages.objective: Allocate resources needed for task execution
stages.input: Task list, deadlines, available resources
stages.activities: Identify resource needs, allocate budget, allocate tools/access, plan support
stages.successMetric: Resource needs identified and allocated
stages.decisionPoints: Resources sufficient? Conflicts? Contingencies needed?

stages.name: Kickoff
stages.objective: Kick off week/month with team alignment
stages.input: Tasks, assignments, resources, deadlines
stages.activities: Hold kickoff meeting, review priorities, clarify tasks, address questions, establish communication cadence
stages.successMetric: Team aligned and ready to execute
stages.decisionPoints: Everyone clear on priorities? Any blockers before start?

stages.name: Progress Tracking
stages.objective: Track daily/weekly progress throughout period
stages.input: Tasks assigned, deadlines set
stages.output: Daily/weekly progress updates and issue escalation
stages.activities: Daily standup (15 min), track progress, identify blockers, escalate issues, adjust plan as needed
stages.tools: Standup tools, task management, issue tracking
stages.successMetric: Daily progress tracked, blockers visible
stages.decisionPoints: On track? Blockers identified? Plan adjustments needed?
stages.qualityGate: Daily tracking happening, issues escalated quickly

stages.name: Adjustment
stages.objective: Adjust execution plan based on real-time learning
stages.input: Progress data, blockers, changes
stages.output: Adjusted plan for remainder of week/month
stages.activities: Assess progress vs. plan, identify adjustments needed, rebalance resources, communicate changes, keep momentum
stages.successMetric: Plan adjusted as needed, team kept on track
stages.decisionPoints: Major adjustments needed? Resource rebalancing? Timeline changes?
stages.qualityGate: Adjustments made quickly, minimal plan disruption

stages.name: Metric Definition
stages.objective: Define which metrics matter for GTM success
stages.input: OKRs, strategy, business goals, customer needs
stages.activities: Identify leading and lagging indicators, define metric names/descriptions, identify owners
stages.roles: Analytics (definition), GTM leadership (strategy input), Finance (business input)
stages.successMetric: 15-20 key metrics defined with descriptions
stages.decisionPoints: Which metrics truly matter? Leading vs. lagging? Actionable?
stages.qualityGate: Metrics defined and agreed as key indicators

stages.name: Data Source Identification
stages.objective: Identify where data comes from for each metric
stages.input: Metric definitions, data systems available
stages.output: Data source mapping for each metric
stages.activities: Identify system where each metric lives (CRM, marketing automation, analytics), confirm data availability, plan data integration
stages.successMetric: Data sources identified for all metrics
stages.decisionPoints: Data available? Clean? Integration needed?

stages.name: Calculation Logic
stages.objective: Define exactly how each metric is calculated
stages.input: Metrics, data sources
stages.activities: Define calculation formula, define data filters/segments, define time periods, document edge cases
stages.successMetric: Calculation logic documented for all metrics
stages.decisionPoints: Logic clear and unambiguous? Consistent across reports?

stages.name: Baseline Setting
stages.objective: Establish baseline for each metric
stages.input: Historical data, calculation logic
stages.activities: Pull historical data, calculate baseline, document baseline assumptions
stages.successMetric: Baselines calculated and documented
stages.decisionPoints: Baseline realistic? Comparable periods?

stages.name: Target Setting
stages.objective: Set targets for each metric
stages.input: Baselines, OKRs, strategy
stages.activities: Set targets based on OKRs and strategy, set committed vs. stretch targets, document rationale
stages.successMetric: Targets set for all metrics for year and quarters
stages.decisionPoints: Targets ambitious but achievable? Aligned to OKRs?

stages.name: Dashboard Creation
stages.objective: Create dashboards to track metrics
stages.input: Metrics, targets, data sources, calculation logic
stages.activities: Design dashboard layout, configure data pulls, set up automated reporting, establish refresh cadence
stages.tools: Dashboard tools (Tableau, Looker, etc.), data integration
stages.successMetric: Dashboards live and updated regularly
stages.decisionPoints: Accessible to right people? Refresh frequency adequate?
stages.qualityGate: Dashboards live and showing accurate data

stages.name: Monitoring
stages.objective: Monitor metrics against targets throughout period
stages.input: Live dashboards, targets
stages.activities: Review metrics vs. targets, identify variances, investigate root causes, communicate results
stages.successMetric: Metrics monitored weekly/monthly with results communicated
stages.decisionPoints: On track to targets? Variances explained? Actions taken?

stages.name: Optimization
stages.objective: Optimize metrics based on performance data
stages.input: Performance data, variance analysis, team feedback
stages.activities: Analyze what's driving underperformance, plan optimizations, adjust targets if needed, implement improvements
stages.successMetric: Metrics reviewed quarterly, optimizations planned
stages.decisionPoints: Targets still realistic? Metrics still relevant? Optimizations possible?
stages.qualityGate: Quarterly metric review and optimization happening

stages.name: Reporting Needs Assessment
stages.objective: Identify who needs what reporting
stages.input: Stakeholder list, decision-making needs
stages.activities: Identify stakeholders (executives, managers, ICs), identify their questions/needs, identify required frequency
stages.successMetric: Reporting requirements documented for each stakeholder group
stages.decisionPoints: Who needs what information? Frequency? Detail level?

stages.name: Metric Selection
stages.objective: Select metrics to include in dashboards/reports
stages.input: Available metrics, stakeholder needs
stages.activities: Select relevant metrics per audience, prioritize by importance, plan data sources
stages.successMetric: Metrics selected for each reporting audience
stages.decisionPoints: Right metrics for audience? Actionable? Too many or too few?
stages.qualityGate: Metrics selected and stakeholders agree relevant

stages.name: Dashboard Design
stages.objective: Design dashboards for each reporting audience
stages.input: Metrics selected, visualization needs, brand guidelines
stages.activities: Design dashboard layout, identify visualizations, design for accessibility, balance comprehensiveness and simplicity
stages.successMetric: Dashboard designs created for each audience
stages.decisionPoints: Layouts intuitive? Visualizations clear? Data hierarchy right?

stages.name: Data Integration
stages.objective: Integrate data sources to populate dashboards
stages.input: Dashboard designs, metric definitions, data sources
stages.activities: Build data queries, configure data pulls, set up transformations, validate data accuracy
stages.successMetric: Dashboards connected to live data
stages.decisionPoints: Data accurate? Refresh frequency sufficient? Data quality good?

stages.name: Automation Setup
stages.objective: Automate dashboard updates and report generation
stages.input: Dashboards live, reporting frequency defined
stages.output: Automated dashboard updates and report generation
stages.activities: Set up automated data refresh, set up automated report generation, schedule deliveries, configure alerts
stages.successMetric: Dashboards auto-update, reports auto-generate
stages.decisionPoints: Refresh frequency adequate? Distribution timing right? Alerts useful?
stages.qualityGate: Automation working, no manual intervention needed

stages.name: Distribution
stages.objective: Get dashboards/reports to stakeholders
stages.input: Automated reports/dashboards
stages.activities: Set up report distribution, provide access to dashboards, communicate cadence, establish access controls
stages.successMetric: Reports distributed on schedule, dashboard access available
stages.decisionPoints: Distribution working? Access correct? Format right?

stages.name: Consumption Tracking
stages.objective: Track whether stakeholders are using reports/dashboards
stages.input: Distributed reports, dashboards available
stages.activities: Track report opens, track dashboard views, identify usage patterns, gather feedback
stages.successMetric: Usage data collected and analyzed
stages.decisionPoints: Usage levels adequate? Engagement high? Gaps in consumption?
stages.qualityGate: Usage tracking in place, patterns visible

stages.name: Refinement
stages.objective: Refine reports and dashboards based on usage and feedback
stages.input: Usage data, stakeholder feedback
stages.activities: Analyze feedback, identify improvements, adjust metrics/visualizations, update dashboards, communicate changes
stages.successMetric: Reports/dashboards refined quarterly based on feedback
stages.decisionPoints: Major changes needed? Metrics still relevant? Format working?
stages.qualityGate: Regular refinement happening, stakeholder satisfaction high

stages.name: Data Audit
stages.objective: Audit current data landscape and quality
stages.input: Data systems in use, current data
stages.output: Data audit report with quality assessment
stages.activities: Inventory data systems, assess data completeness, assess data accuracy, identify quality issues, identify gaps
stages.tools: Data auditing tools, data quality tools
stages.successMetric: Comprehensive data audit completed
stages.decisionPoints: Data quality issues identified? Extent of problems? Priority fixes?
stages.qualityGate: Data audit completed and issues documented

stages.name: Quality Issues Identification
stages.objective: Identify specific data quality problems
stages.input: Data audit, quality assessment
stages.output: Prioritized list of data quality issues
stages.activities: Categorize issues (duplicates, missing data, incorrect data), prioritize by impact, estimate effort to fix
stages.successMetric: Quality issues identified and prioritized
stages.decisionPoints: Which issues most important? Quick wins available? Root causes?

stages.name: Data Governance Plan
stages.objective: Create plan for managing data quality going forward
stages.input: Quality issues identified, organizational structure
stages.output: Data governance plan with policies and responsibilities
stages.activities: Define data governance policies, assign data owners, define data quality standards, define escalation process
stages.successMetric: Comprehensive data governance plan documented
stages.decisionPoints: Roles clear? Standards realistic? Enforcement mechanisms?

stages.name: Integration Setup
stages.objective: Integrate data systems to ensure consistency
stages.input: Data systems inventory, integration needs
stages.activities: Map data across systems, build data pipelines, configure automated syncs, test integrations
stages.tools: Data integration tools (Zapier, make.com, etc.), APIs
stages.successMetric: Key data integrations configured and working
stages.decisionPoints: Integration coverage sufficient? Sync frequency adequate? Error handling?

stages.name: Validation Rules
stages.objective: Implement validation rules to prevent bad data
stages.input: Data quality standards, data entry points
stages.activities: Define validation rules, configure in systems, test rules, provide feedback to users
stages.tools: Data validation tools, CRM configuration, automation
stages.successMetric: Validation rules implemented across key systems
stages.decisionPoints: Rules comprehensive? Too restrictive? User experience?
stages.qualityGate: Validation rules working and preventing bad data

stages.name: Ongoing Monitoring
stages.objective: Monitor data quality on ongoing basis
stages.input: Data systems with validation, metrics defined
stages.activities: Monitor data quality metrics, identify new issues early, escalate problems, provide feedback to data owners
stages.successMetric: Data quality monitored monthly with visibility
stages.decisionPoints: Quality improving? New issues appearing? Root causes?
stages.qualityGate: Monitoring system in place, monthly reports generated

stages.name: Regular Audits
stages.objective: Conduct regular audits of data quality and governance
stages.input: Data quality metrics, governance policies
stages.activities: Conduct data quality audits, assess governance compliance, identify improvement areas
stages.successMetric: Quarterly audits conducted, results documented
stages.decisionPoints: Quality improving? Governance being followed? Major issues?

stages.name: Improvement
stages.objective: Continuously improve data quality and governance
stages.input: Audit results, monitoring data, issue feedback
stages.activities: Plan improvements, execute fixes, retrain users, document learnings
stages.successMetric: Data quality improving over time, governance compliance high
stages.decisionPoints: Most important improvements? Quick wins? Training needed?
stages.qualityGate: Improvement plan executed, quality metrics show improvement

stages.name: Touch Point Definition
stages.objective: Define all customer touch points to track
stages.input: Customer journey, marketing channels, sales activities
stages.activities: Map customer journey, identify all touch points (ads, content, sales calls, events, etc.), plan tracking for each
stages.successMetric: All major touch points identified
stages.decisionPoints: Which touch points matter? Tracking feasible? Data available?
stages.qualityGate: Touch point list comprehensive and tracking feasible

stages.name: Attribution Model Design
stages.objective: Design attribution model (how credit gets assigned to touch points)
stages.input: Touch points, customer data, business goals
stages.activities: Choose model type (first-touch, last-touch, linear, time-decay, custom), specify model rules, get stakeholder agreement
stages.successMetric: Attribution model designed and documented
stages.decisionPoints: Which model best reflects business? Stakeholder agreement? Custom needed?
stages.qualityGate: Model specified, stakeholders agree on approach

stages.name: Data Collection Setup
stages.objective: Set up systems to collect attribution data
stages.input: Attribution model, touch points, data systems
stages.activities: Implement tracking code, configure analytics, set up CRM tracking, set up integration between systems
stages.tools: Analytics platforms, UTM tracking, CRM, data integration
stages.successMetric: Data collection working for all touch points
stages.decisionPoints: Tracking complete? Data flowing correctly? Quality good?

stages.name: Analysis Framework
stages.objective: Define framework for analyzing attribution data
stages.input: Attribution model, business questions, available tools
stages.activities: Define key questions to answer (which channels drive revenue, what's CAC by channel, etc.), plan analysis approach
stages.successMetric: Analysis framework documented
stages.decisionPoints: Right questions? Feasible to analyze? Tools adequate?

stages.name: Campaign Attribution
stages.objective: Calculate attribution for each marketing campaign
stages.input: Attribution model, campaign data, touch point data
stages.activities: Analyze which touch points contributed to conversions, calculate credit per campaign, identify highest-impact campaigns
stages.tools: Analytics platforms, attribution tools, BI tools
stages.successMetric: Campaign attribution reports generated
stages.decisionPoints: Which campaigns most impactful? Surprising results? Actionable insights?

stages.name: ROI Calculation
stages.objective: Calculate ROI by campaign/channel
stages.input: Campaign attribution, campaign spend, customer value
stages.activities: Calculate revenue influenced by campaign, compare to campaign spend, calculate ROI, identify most efficient channels
stages.tools: Financial tools, ROI calculators, BI tools
stages.successMetric: ROI calculated for all major campaigns/channels
stages.decisionPoints: Which channels most efficient? ROI meeting targets? Budget allocation optimal?

stages.name: Optimization
stages.objective: Optimize marketing spend based on attribution and ROI
stages.input: Attribution and ROI data, campaign performance
stages.activities: Identify highest-ROI channels, identify lowest-ROI channels, plan budget shifts, plan performance improvements
stages.successMetric: Attribution insights used to optimize spending
stages.decisionPoints: Which channels shift budget to? Should we stop underperformers? Invest in winners?
stages.qualityGate: Attribution insights regularly used to optimize spending

stages.name: Decision Type Definition
stages.objective: Identify types of decisions that get made in GTM
stages.input: Strategy, organizational structure, common decisions
stages.activities: Identify strategic decisions, identify tactical decisions, identify operational decisions, categorize decisions
stages.successMetric: Decision types categorized
stages.decisionPoints: Right categories? Overlaps? Mutually exclusive?

stages.name: Authority Mapping
stages.objective: Map authority to make decisions to roles/individuals
stages.input: Decision types, organizational structure, decision value/impact
stages.activities: Assign decision authority by type, define escalation thresholds, identify veto power, document exceptions
stages.successMetric: Clear authority matrix documented
stages.decisionPoints: Authority clear? Aligned to organizational structure? Fair distribution?

stages.name: Process Documentation
stages.objective: Document decision-making process
stages.input: Authority matrix, decision types
stages.activities: Document process for each decision type, identify inputs/stakeholders, identify timeline, document documentation requirements
stages.successMetric: Decision process documented for all decision types
stages.decisionPoints: Processes clear? Efficiently designed? Properly documented?

stages.name: Training
stages.objective: Train team on decision-making framework
stages.input: Authority matrix, process documentation
stages.activities: Hold training session, review authority matrix, review decision processes, answer questions, test understanding
stages.successMetric: Team trained on decision framework
stages.decisionPoints: Team understanding? Questions resolved? Adoption likely?
stages.qualityGate: Training complete, team ready to use framework

stages.name: Execution
stages.objective: Execute decisions following the framework
stages.input: Decision type identified, framework in place
stages.activities: Identify decision type, gather inputs, get appropriate approval, document decision, communicate
stages.successMetric: Decisions made and documented systematically
stages.decisionPoints: Process being followed? Decisions efficient? Stakeholder buy-in?

stages.name: Review
stages.objective: Review decision outcomes
stages.input: Decision made, results over time
stages.activities: Review decision against objectives, assess if it achieved intended outcome, document learnings
stages.successMetric: Decisions reviewed for outcome
stages.decisionPoints: Decision effective? What worked? What didn't?

stages.name: Feedback Loop
stages.objective: Gather feedback on decision-making process
stages.input: Decision outcomes, process execution
stages.activities: Gather feedback from decision-makers, gather feedback from stakeholders, identify process improvements
stages.successMetric: Feedback collected regularly
stages.decisionPoints: Process working well? Improvements needed? Changes to framework?

stages.name: Refinement
stages.objective: Refine decision framework based on learning
stages.input: Feedback, outcome assessments
stages.activities: Identify framework improvements, update authority/process as needed, retrain team, communicate changes
stages.successMetric: Framework refined regularly, improvements implemented
stages.decisionPoints: Framework improvements clear? Should we change authority? Process refinements?
stages.qualityGate: Annual framework review and refinement happening

stages.name: Status Collection
stages.objective: Gather status updates from all teams
stages.input: Initiative progress, team accomplishments, blockers
stages.activities: Have team leads provide updates (what we accomplished, what we're working on, blockers), consolidate status
stages.successMetric: Status received from all teams
stages.decisionPoints: What was accomplished? What's on track?

stages.name: Issue Identification
stages.objective: Identify issues that need discussion/resolution
stages.input: Status updates, team feedback
stages.activities: Identify blockers, identify risks, identify decisions needed, prioritize issues
stages.successMetric: Issues identified and prioritized
stages.decisionPoints: Which issues most urgent? What can be resolved quickly?

stages.name: Discussion
stages.objective: Discuss issues and get team input
stages.input: Issue list, team input
stages.activities: Facilitate discussion, get diverse perspectives, understand root causes, explore solutions
stages.successMetric: Issues discussed thoroughly
stages.decisionPoints: Root causes clear? Possible solutions identified?

stages.name: Decision Making
stages.objective: Make decisions to resolve issues
stages.input: Issue discussion, authority matrix
stages.activities: Make decisions on issues, assign accountability, set timelines
stages.successMetric: Decisions made on all critical issues
stages.decisionPoints: Decision clear? Owner assigned? Timeline realistic?

stages.name: Action Items
stages.objective: Document action items from standup
stages.input: Decisions made, discussion outcomes
stages.output: Documented action items with owners and deadlines
stages.activities: Capture action items, assign owners, set deadlines, document in issue tracking system
stages.successMetric: All action items documented and assigned
stages.decisionPoints: All items captured? Owners confirmed? Deadlines realistic?

stages.name: Follow-up
stages.objective: Follow up on action items during the week
stages.input: Action items assigned
stages.output: Action item progress through the week
stages.activities: Check in on action items mid-week, escalate anything at risk, provide support to owners
stages.successMetric: Action items tracked to completion
stages.decisionPoints: On track to deadline? Support needed? Blockers?

stages.name: Resolution
stages.objective: Close out action items when complete
stages.input: Completed action items
stages.activities: Confirm completion, document resolution, communicate outcomes
stages.successMetric: Action items closed when complete
stages.decisionPoints: Completion acceptable? Learning captured?

stages.name: Learning Capture
stages.objective: Capture learnings for improvement
stages.input: Issues discussed, resolutions, outcomes
stages.activities: Identify patterns in issues, document root causes, capture best practices
stages.successMetric: Learnings documented monthly
stages.decisionPoints: Patterns in issues? Systemic problems? Improvement opportunities?

stages.name: Strategy Review
stages.objective: Review annual strategy and assess relevance to current quarter
stages.input: Annual GTM strategy, prior quarter results, market changes, competitive updates
activities: Review annual strategy and strategic pillars
Assess if strategy still applies given market/competitive changes
Review last quarter results and learnings
Identify if strategic adjustments needed
Document any strategic pivots or adjustments
stages.successMetric: Strategy confirmed or adjusted, documented for quarter planning
decisionPoints: Does our annual strategy still make sense?
Should we pivot based on last quarter learnings?
Are market conditions changing our strategy?

qualityGate.go: Go if: Strategy reviewed and confirmed, any pivots documented and approved
qualityGate.loopback: Loop back if: Major strategy questions, need executive alignment

stages.name: Objective Setting
stages.objective: Define quarterly objectives and key results (OKRs)
stages.input: Strategy confirmed, budget available, team capacity
stages.output: Quarterly OKRs (3-5 objectives with 3-4 key results each)
activities: Define quarterly objectives (what do we want to achieve?)
Set key results for each objective (how do we measure success?)
Balance committed vs. stretch goals
Set targets that are ambitious but achievable
Get alignment from all teams on OKRs
roles: Team leads: input on ambitious-but-achievable targets
stages.successMetric: 3-5 quarterly OKRs with clear key results defined and approved
decisionPoints: What are our top 3-5 priorities for the quarter?
Are our targets stretching but realistic?
Do we have dependencies between OKRs?

qualityGate.go: Go if: OKRs approved by leadership, teams understand and committed
qualityGate.loopback: Loop back if: OKRs too ambitious/conservative, need recalibration

stages.name: Initiative Planning
stages.objective: Identify specific initiatives needed to achieve OKRs
stages.input: Quarterly OKRs, team capacity, available budget
stages.output: List of initiatives with owners, timelines, budgets
activities: Identify initiatives needed to achieve each OKR
Define initiative scope, timeline, and success criteria
Estimate resource requirements (headcount, budget, tools)
Identify dependencies between initiatives
Assign owners and executive sponsors
Sequence initiatives throughout quarter
stages.tools: Project management tools, initiative planning templates
roles: Team leads: initiative identification and planning
stages.successMetric: List of initiatives defined with owners, timelines, budgets
decisionPoints: Which initiatives are most critical?
Do we have capacity to execute all initiatives?
Should we prioritize or parallelize?

qualityGate.go: Go if: All initiatives assigned owners, budgets approved, sequencing clear
qualityGate.loopback: Loop back if: Too many initiatives, resource constraints, need to prioritize

stages.name: Resource Allocation
stages.objective: Allocate budget and headcount to initiatives
stages.input: Initiatives list, available budget, headcount available
stages.output: Resource allocation plan with budget by initiative
activities: Allocate budget by initiative (how much can we spend on each?)
Allocate headcount by initiative (who is working on what?)
Identify any resource gaps (what do we need vs. what do we have?)
Plan for new hiring if needed
Document resource constraints and trade-offs
stages.tools: Budget tracking, HRIS, resource planning tools
stages.successMetric: Budget allocated by initiative, resource plan documented
decisionPoints: Are we over-resourced on any initiatives?
Are we under-resourced on critical initiatives?
Should we hire or redirect existing resources?

qualityGate.go: Go if: Budget approved, resource plan clear, no critical gaps
qualityGate.loopback: Loop back if: Budget constraints force priority changes, need executive decision

stages.name: Team Alignment
stages.objective: Ensure all teams understand quarterly priorities and plan
stages.input: OKRs, initiatives, resource allocation
activities: Hold kickoff meeting with extended team
Present OKRs and explain rationale
Present initiatives and resource allocations
Address questions and concerns
Establish communication cadence for quarter
Distribute planning documents to all teams
roles: GTM leadership: kickoff facilitation and communication
stages.successMetric: Team kickoff completed, plan communicated, teams aligned and committed
decisionPoints: Do teams understand the quarterly priorities?
Are there any unresolved concerns or questions?
Is everyone committed to the plan?

qualityGate.go: Go if: Kickoff completed, Q&A addressed, teams ready to execute
qualityGate.loopback: Loop back if: Significant resistance or unclear understanding, need more alignment

stages.name: Execution Kickoff
stages.objective: Launch initiatives and establish execution cadence
stages.input: Teams aligned, budgets approved, resource allocated
stages.output: Initiatives kicked off with tracking and governance in place
activities: Kick off each initiative (project planning, team assignment)
